articles.title: Dolphins to release Tua, take on record cap hit
articles.summary: The Dolphins will release quarterback Tua Tagovailoa after the start of the new league year in a move that will leave Miami with an NFL-record $99 million in dead money.

articles.title: Sources: Rams reach record deal with McDuffie
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams and All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie reached agreement on a record four-year, $124 million extension that includes $100 million guaranteed, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Sunday night.

articles.title: Raiders trading for Bills CB Johnson, source says
articles.summary: The Raiders are sending a sixth-round pick to the Bills in exchange for veteran cornerback Taron Johnson and a seventh-round selection, a source told ESPN.

articles.title: Source: Bengals won't tender backup QB Browning
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are not tendering restricted free agent quarterback Jake Browning, who started 10 games over three seasons in relief of Joe Burrow, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

articles.title: Sources: Ingram back to Texans on 3-year deal
articles.summary: Texans guard Ed Ingram will not hit free agency after agreeing to return to Houston on a three-year, $37.5 million deal, according to ESPN and NFL Network.

articles.title: Steelers to bring back CB Samuel, sources say
articles.summary: The Steelers are re-signing corner Asante Samuel Jr. to a one-year, $4 million deal, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

articles.title: Sources: Conner reworks deal to stay with Cards
articles.summary: The Cardinals and Pro Bowl running back James Conner have agreed to a revised contract to keep him in Arizona for 2026, according to NFL Network.

articles.title: Source: Wilson sticks with Vikings after big year
articles.summary: Linebacker Eric Wilson is staying with the Minnesota Vikings, as the sides agreed to a three-year, $22.5 million contract Sunday ahead of NFL free agency, according to NFL Network.

articles.title: FB Ingold joins Chargers, reunites with McDaniel
articles.summary: The Chargers agreed to terms on a contract with fullback Alec Ingold, reuniting him with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.
